[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Multi-Tenancy, Namespaces, and Resource Quotas in Kubernetes"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"As Kubernetes clusters scale to support multiple teams, applications, or business units, maintaining isolation and resource fairness becomes a critical challenge. Multi-tenancy allows organizations to share a single Kubernetes cluster securely while keeping tenants isolated from one another."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Understanding Kubernetes Namespaces"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Namespaces provide a mechanism for isolating groups of resources within a single cluster. They act as virtual clusters inside your physical Kubernetes cluster, providing a scope for names and resource allocation."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Default namespaces include default, kube-system, and kube-public, which are automatically created during cluster initialization."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Namespaces provide scope for names. Names of resources need only be unique within a namespace, not across the entire cluster."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"They form the foundation for implementing security boundaries and resource governance."},{"order":8,"type":"subheading","text":"Creating and Managing Namespaces"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"You can create a namespace using either a declarative YAML configuration file or directly via the kubectl command line interface."},{"order":10,"type":"code","text":"kubectl create namespace team-alpha"},{"order":11,"type":"paragraph","text":"Alternatively, define a namespace manifest named 'namespace-alpha.yaml':"},{"order":12,"type":"code","text":"apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: team-alpha"},{"order":13,"type":"subheading","text":"Implementing Resource Quotas"},{"order":14,"type":"paragraph","text":"While namespaces isolate resources by name, they do not restrict resource consumption by default. Without limits, a single tenant can monopolize cluster CPU and memory. ResourceQuotas solve this by limiting aggregate resource consumption per namespace."},{"order":15,"type":"paragraph","text":"Here is an example of a ResourceQuota configuration file named 'quota-alpha.yaml' that restricts CPU, memory, and pod counts for the 'team-alpha' namespace:"},{"order":16,"type":"code","text":"apiVersion: v1
kind: ResourceQuota
metadata:
  name: compute-resources
  namespace: team-alpha
spec:
  hard:
    requests.cpu: "4"
    requests.memory: "8Gi"
    limits.cpu: "8"
    limits.memory: "16Gi"
    pods: "20""},{"order":17,"type":"paragraph","text":"Apply the quota to your cluster using the following command:"},{"order":18,"type":"code","text":"kubectl apply -f quota-alpha.yaml"},{"order":19,"type":"subheading","text":"Limit Ranges for Defaulting and Minimums"},{"order":20,"type":"paragraph","text":"ResourceQuotas govern total consumption, but LimitRanges dictate constraints on individual pods or containers within a namespace. LimitRanges can enforce minimum and maximum resource constraints, as well as set default request and limit values for containers that do not explicitly specify them."},{"order":21,"type":"code","text":"apiVersion: v1
kind: LimitRange
metadata:
  name: cpu-memory-limits
  namespace: team-alpha
spec:
  limits:
  - default:
      cpu: "500m"
      memory: "512Mi"
    defaultRequest:
      cpu: "200m"
      memory: "256Mi"
    type: Container"},{"order":22,"type":"subheading","text":"Best Practices for Multi-Tenancy"},{"order":23,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Always pair namespaces with ResourceQuotas and LimitRanges to prevent resource exhaustion."},{"order":24,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Use NetworkPolicies to restrict pod-to-pod communication across different namespaces."},{"order":25,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Leverage Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) to restrict tenant users to their respective namespaces."}]
